summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Doxo to pay $2.1M settlement
articles.description: The online bill-pay company agreed to settle a case brought by the Federal Trade Commission over deceptive ads and undisclosed fees.

articles.title: Klarna’s growth hits speed bump
articles.description: The buy now, pay later player won’t live up to its financial forecast for this year because of a slowdown in one of its largest markets.

articles.title: Citi scoops up card rewards firm
articles.description: The New York startup Kard has technology, talent and merchant ties that the bank expects will strengthen a loyalty strategy for its consumer cards business.

articles.title: Western Union navigates challenges
articles.description: The company is dealing with turmoil from the shift to digital money transfers as it seeks regulatory approvals for a $500 million deal for rival Intermex.

articles.title: How state payments oversight skids
articles.description: “In the absence of a federal consumer privacy framework, both consumers and businesses are paying the price,” one company founder writes.

articles.title: Credit card strain rises: study
articles.description: As consumers spend more on their credit cards, some cardholders are carrying hefty balances, a J.D. Power analysis found.

articles.title: Sezzle pivots to national bank charter
articles.description: With states imposing tighter rules on buy now, pay later companies, Sezzle CEO Charlie Youakim views a federal charter as “the most robust solution.”

articles.title: Cash lags credit, debit payments
articles.description: Though most consumers prefer debit and credit card payments, 90% say they’ll still use cash for the foreseeable future, a Fed survey finds.
